# AWS IoT Rule Events

The `iot` event invokes a Lambda function when devices publish MQTT messages to AWS IoT Core. For each `iot` event, the Framework creates an AWS IoT topic rule whose SQL statement selects the messages and a Lambda action that passes the result to your function. Use it to process device telemetry or react to device messages; to run code while a device is being provisioned, use [IoT fleet provisioning events](./iot-fleet-provisioning.md) instead.

The following `serverless.yml` invokes the `ingest` function for every message published to a topic under `sensors/`:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-iot-service

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  ingest:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iot:
          sql: "SELECT * FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry'"
          sqlVersion: '2016-03-23'
```

Quote the whole statement in YAML and put the topic filter in single quotes inside it, as AWS IoT SQL requires. `sqlVersion` is optional, but AWS IoT uses `2015-10-08` without it, and AWS recommends `2016-03-23` (see [SQL version](#sql-version-sqlversion)).

## `iot` event settings

The `iot` event takes an object with these keys:

| Key           | Type    | Default                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sql`         | String  | Required                    | The rule's [AWS IoT SQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-sql-reference.html) statement: `SELECT` fields `FROM` a topic filter, with an optional `WHERE` condition. |
| `sqlVersion`  | String  | AWS default `2015-10-08`    | The SQL rules engine version: `2015-10-08`, `2016-03-23` or `beta`.                                                                                                                          |
| `name`        | String  | Generated by CloudFormation | The rule name. Letters, digits and underscores only, 1 to 128 characters.                                                                                                                    |
| `description` | String  | None                        | The rule description.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `enabled`     | Boolean | `true`                      | Whether the rule runs. `false` deploys the rule disabled.                                                                                                                                    |

A function can have several `iot` events; each creates its own rule and permission.

## SQL statement (`sql`)

The `iot` event's `sql` decides which messages invoke the function and what the function receives. The `FROM` clause is an MQTT topic filter, where `+` matches one topic level and `#` matches all remaining levels; `WHERE` filters messages. The following event invokes the function only for readings above 50 and passes two fields, the message's `temperature` and the device ID from the topic:

```yaml
functions:
  ingest:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iot:
          sql: "SELECT temperature, topic(2) AS deviceId FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry' WHERE temperature > 50"
          sqlVersion: '2016-03-23'
```

The AWS IoT SQL function [`topic(N)`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-sql-functions.html#iot-function-topic) returns level `N` of the topic the message arrived on, counting from 1, and `topic()` returns the whole topic. For a message published to `sensors/device-42/telemetry`, `topic(2)` is `device-42`. To pass the whole message and add the device ID, select `*` with it: `SELECT *, topic(2) AS deviceId FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry' WHERE temperature > 50`.

The Framework removes line breaks from `sql` without adding spaces. To split a long statement over several lines, use a YAML folded block (`sql: >`), which joins the lines with spaces.

## SQL version (`sqlVersion`)

The `iot` event's `sqlVersion` selects the [AWS IoT SQL rules engine version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-rule-sql-version.html):

- `2016-03-23`: recommended by AWS; adds nested object queries and fixes for nested JSON and array queries.
- `2015-10-08`: the original version, and the one AWS IoT uses when `sqlVersion` is omitted.
- `beta`: the most recent beta version, which can introduce breaking changes.

Changing `sqlVersion` updates the rule in place.

## Rule name and description

To give the rule a fixed name, set the `iot` event's `name`; to label it in the AWS IoT console, set `description`:

```yaml
functions:
  ingest:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iot:
          name: sensors_telemetry_ingest
          description: Sends sensor telemetry to the ingest function
          sql: "SELECT * FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry'"
```

AWS IoT rule names allow only letters, digits and underscores, up to 128 characters, and are unique per account and Region, so include the stage in the name when you deploy several stages to one account (for example `sensors_ingest_${sls:stage}`, with a stage name that has no hyphens). Without `name`, CloudFormation generates a unique name from the stack and resource names. Changing `name` replaces the rule. The Framework removes line breaks from `name` and `description`.

## Disable an IoT rule

To stop the rule from invoking the function without removing it, set the `iot` event's `enabled` to `false`:

```yaml
functions:
  ingest:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iot:
          sql: "SELECT * FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry'"
          enabled: false
```

The rule stays deployed in a disabled state. Set `enabled` back to `true`, or remove the key, and deploy again to turn it on.

## AWS resources and permissions for `iot` events

For each `iot` event, the Framework adds two resources to the stack:

- An `AWS::IoT::TopicRule` with the logical ID `<FunctionName>IotTopicRule<N>` (for example `IngestIotTopicRule1`). Its only action is a Lambda action that targets the function, or the function's alias when the function uses `provisionedConcurrency`, [SnapStart](../guide/functions.md#snapstart) or [durable functions](../guide/functions.md#durable-functions).
- An `AWS::Lambda::Permission` with the logical ID `<FunctionName>LambdaPermissionIotTopicRule<N>`, which lets the principal `iot.amazonaws.com` call `lambda:InvokeFunction`, with the source ARN set to that rule's ARN.

The function's execution role needs no extra permissions for this event. The Framework doesn't create things, certificates or AWS IoT policies; devices need their own [AWS IoT policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-policies.html) that allow `iot:Publish` to the topics the rule reads.

The logical IDs start with the function name, with its first letter in uppercase, `-` replaced by `Dash` and `_` by `Underscore`: the first `iot` event of a function named `hot-readings` creates `HotDashreadingsIotTopicRule1`.

## Error action for an IoT rule

AWS IoT runs a rule's [error action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/rule-error-handling.html) when it can't complete one of the rule's actions, for example when it can't invoke the function. The `iot` event has no error action key: it accepts only the keys in [`iot` event settings](#iot-event-settings). To add an error action, define the rule under `resources.Resources` with its logical ID, its `Type` and only `ErrorAction`. The Framework merges that definition into the rule it generates, so the rule keeps its SQL statement and Lambda action.

The following `serverless.yml` sends the messages that the `ingest` function's first `iot` rule can't deliver to an SQS queue, through an IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to call `sqs:SendMessage`:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-iot-service

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  ingest:
    handler: handler.handler
    events:
      - iot:
          sql: "SELECT *, topic(2) AS deviceId FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry' WHERE temperature > 30"
          sqlVersion: '2016-03-23'

resources:
  Resources:
    IngestIotTopicRule1:
      Type: AWS::IoT::TopicRule
      Properties:
        TopicRulePayload:
          ErrorAction:
            Sqs:
              QueueUrl: !Ref IotErrorQueue
              RoleArn: !GetAtt IotErrorActionRole.Arn
    IotErrorQueue:
      Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    IotErrorActionRole:
      Type: AWS::IAM::Role
      Properties:
        AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              Principal:
                Service: iot.amazonaws.com
              Action: sts:AssumeRole
        Policies:
          - PolicyName: iot-error-action
            PolicyDocument:
              Version: '2012-10-17'
              Statement:
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action: sqs:SendMessage
                  Resource: !GetAtt IotErrorQueue.Arn
```

The queue receives one message per failed rule run, with the rule name, the topic, the Base64-encoded original payload and the failures, in the [error action message format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/rule-error-handling.html#rule-error-message-format). The SQS action can't send to FIFO queues.

Errors the function throws don't trigger the error action. AWS IoT invokes the function asynchronously, and Lambda accepts the event before the function runs, so Lambda retries a failed invocation and can send it to a failure destination. Configure that with the function's `destinations.onFailure` and `maximumRetryAttempts`, described in [asynchronous invocation](../guide/functions.md#asynchronous-invocation).

## Event payload from an AWS IoT rule

AWS IoT invokes the function [asynchronously](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/lambda-rule-action.html), so the function's return value is discarded and Lambda's [asynchronous invocation](../guide/functions.md#asynchronous-invocation) retry and destination settings apply. The event is the output of the rule's SQL statement, not the raw MQTT message. For example, with the rule `SELECT *, topic(2) AS deviceId FROM 'sensors/+/telemetry' WHERE temperature > 30`, this message published to `sensors/device-42/telemetry`:

```json
{
  "temperature": 34.5,
  "humidity": 40
}
```

invokes the function with this event:

```json
{
  "temperature": 34.5,
  "humidity": 40,
  "deviceId": "device-42"
}
```

A message with `temperature` of 30 or lower doesn't invoke the function.

The following `handler.mjs` logs each event it receives:

```javascript
// handler.mjs
export const handler = async (event) => {
  console.log('Message from AWS IoT:', JSON.stringify(event))
}
```

To send a test message, use the MQTT test client in the AWS IoT console and publish to a topic that matches the rule's topic filter.
